absent: Internal byte and record queue helpers for alloc, free, init, in, out, peek, skip, length, user copy, DMA and linear extents including return values and error codes.
Queue front type layout, size and mask and element size derivation, power of two enforcement, and pointer versus embedded storage discrimination.
Spinlock acquisition semantics, interrupt flag handling, memory ordering beyond single element barriers, and required locking protocol for concurrent producers and consumers.
Scatterlist construction, DMA address handling, mapping error behavior, and user memory fault and partial copy semantics.
Reference counted list add, remove, iteration, and get versus put callback contracts and locking rules.
Object and set lifecycle including creation, sysfs attachment, reference counting, uevent emission, filtering and naming, namespace interaction, and ownership.
String parser base handling, overflow and format errors, and user buffer length limits and fault behavior.

findings.text: Occupancy helpers report queue fill without mutating it. Reset discards pending content by aligning consumer position with producer position. Length reflects producer minus consumer distance. Empty holds when the two positions match. Full holds when length exceeds the index mask. Available space subtracts length from total capacity and, for record mode, reserves header space and rounds down to whole records, returning zero when insufficient.

Consumer side discard and inspection distinguish byte and record modes via element record size. Counted skip advances by record header in record mode and by caller count otherwise, with single skip as count one. Length peek returns total byte occupancy in byte mode and next record payload length in record mode, with result checking enforced by helper wrapper.

Lifecycle helpers bind a typed front object to raw storage. Allocation and node aware allocation succeed only for pointer flavor and otherwise report invalid argument, delegating to internal allocators with element size and allocation flags. Free releases only pointer flavor storage. Init attaches caller supplied buffer with size and element size, likewise restricted to pointer flavor.

Single element transfer preserves type through const and pointer views. Put inserts one value and reports acceptance, get removes one value into caller pointer and reports transfer, peek copies head value without advancing and reports presence. Record mode delegates to record helpers. Byte mode checks full or empty first, indexes storage by producer or consumer position masked to capacity, orders data before index update with write barrier, then advances the respective index. Storage selection depends on pointer versus embedded array flavor.

Bulk transfer moves caller buffer contents in elements or bytes. Input and output each select record or byte internal helper according to record size. Checked helper enforces result use on output path. Variants exist for direct call and for calls serialized by caller supplied spinlock, with irq saving, non irq saving, and locked alias forms.

Cross domain transfer covers user memory, scatterlist DMA, and contiguous inspection. From user and to user each dispatch to record or byte internal helpers with length and copied count. DMA input and output prepare build scatterlists for free or occupied space with mapped address variant and default unmapped alias using mapping error sentinel. DMA input finish advances producer by transferred bytes divided by element size or via record helper, DMA output finish discards via counted skip similarly scaled. Non destructive bulk peek, linear extent query with tail output, and linear pointer resolution expose head data without consuming it.

Spinlocked wrappers serialize emptiness checks and bulk moves with a caller supplied lock. Irq saving forms preserve interrupt state across the critical section, non irq saving forms use plain acquire and release and require caller to manage interrupt context. Locked aliases are equivalent to irq saving forms. Underlying unsynchronized primitives remain unsafe for concurrent producers or consumers.

Queue positions are monotonically increasing counters with capacity one more than mask, implying power of two sizing. Occupancy is producer minus consumer using unsigned wrap. Indexing masks position to physical slot. Record mode occupancy and availability are expressed in records with header overhead, byte mode in elements. Write barriers separate slot store or load from index advance for single element paths.

Reference counted list comprises container, node and iterator. Container holds spinlock, head list, and get plus put callbacks, aligned to pointer width. Node holds opaque container backpointer never accessed directly, list linkage, and reference count. Iterator holds owning container pointer and current node pointer.
Static initialization provides unlocked spinlock, empty list head, and caller supplied reference callbacks. Named definition macro creates a container instance from the initializer.

Core object embeds identity, hierarchy, type and lifetime. Fields include name string, sibling entry, parent pointer, set pointer, type pointer, sysfs node, reference count, and five single bit flags for initialized, sysfs presence, add event sent, remove event sent, and event suppression, plus optional delayed release work under debug release configuration.

Type and event descriptors separate behavior from instance. Type carries release callback, sysfs operations, default attribute groups, namespace type lookup, namespace lookup, and ownership query. Event environment carries fixed argument vector, environment pointer array with index, and linear buffer with length. Set operations carry filter, name and event callbacks. Attribute pairs base attribute with show and store handlers each in mutable and const forms.

Small accessors expose name, container conversion and reference handling. Name returns stored string. Set conversion derives enclosing set from embedded object with null tolerance. Set get acquires reference via object get and converts, set put releases via object put. Type accessor returns stored type pointer.
Set groups objects with membership list, list spinlock, embedded object, and set event operations pointer, with randomized layout hardening.

User event limits are fixed numeric capacities: helper path length two hundred fifty six, environment pointer count sixty four, variable buffer two thousand forty eight bytes. Environment structure dimensions derive from the latter two.
Object action enumeration orders lifecycle events as add, remove, change, move, online, offline, bind, unbind with sequential values starting at zero.
Namespace type enumeration defines none as zero, net as one, and count sentinel as two, establishing exactly one valid namespace type beyond none.
Namespace type operations bundle type tag with callbacks for mount permission check, current namespace grab, socket namespace lookup, initial namespace lookup, and namespace release.

Attribute construction derives name string, validates octal permissions, and selects mutable versus const handler slots via generic dispatch on handler type. Convenience forms fix read only, read write, write only, and mode parameterized variants using suffixed show and store symbols, with two build variants differing in const handler representation.

Object event state progresses from add through online and offline and bind and unbind transitions with change and move as mutation notices and remove as terminal withdrawal, tracked by initialized, sysfs presence and add and remove sent flags plus suppression control.

String to integer helpers adapt width and trust domain. Unsigned long and long parsing short circuit to sixty four bit helpers when size and alignment match, otherwise use narrower internal parsers. Fixed width sixty four and thirty two bit signed and unsigned forms delegate to long long or int helpers. From user variants accept user pointer with length and delegate similarly. All report mandatory checked status.

Doubly linked head invariant is self reference when empty. Static and dynamic initializers establish next and previous pointing to head itself using ordered writes. Guarded definition annotates head with associated lock for static analysis.

Insertion validation distinguishes debug and hardened builds. When list debugging is disabled, fast path accepts when predecessor and successor remain mutually linked and new entry differs from both, otherwise defers to reporting helper. Slow path annotation varies by configuration between empty and cold preserve most attributes. Null predecessor or successor need not be checked explicitly because immediate dereference faults.

Several queue uses require external coordination. Reset, skip and DMA finish mutate indices without locking or bounds validation and can discard or fabricate occupancy if raced or over advanced. Full detection relies on mask comparison so non power of two capacity breaks wrap. Byte scaling by division truncates partial elements. Record versus byte selection hinges on record type size so mismatched type yields wrong path.

Reference and hierarchy handling has sharp edges. Node backpointer must never be dereferenced directly. Set put assumes non null set unlike get and container conversion. Attribute permission validation and handler constness rely on compile time generic selection with divergent build variants. List validation fast path is skipped entirely when debugging is enabled, changing diagnostic coverage.
Byte allocator entry forwards size, element size and allocation flags to node aware allocator with no affinity, serving as default placement wrapper.
Header inclusion guards define private macros for klist, kobject, namespace, string conversion and list headers, ensuring single inclusion.
External ordered write primitive used during list head initialization.
External container address derivation used for set conversion.
External configuration query used to select list validation path.
